market_question: Will US withdraw from NATO before 2027?
reasoning: A formal U.S. withdrawal from NATO requires a presidential decision to submit a notice of denunciation under Article 13, which faces massive political, military, and Congressional obstacles. Even under a Trump presidency, this step was never taken during 2017-2021, and bipartisan support for NATO remains strong. The 2-year window (2025-2026) is too short for such a radical shift, making a withdrawal extremely unlikely.
evidence_points: No U.S. president has ever submitted a notice of withdrawal from NATO, despite occasional criticism of burden-sharing.
Congress passed the NATO Support Act in 2019 (bipartisan) and could block or defund a withdrawal through legislation.
Trump's first term saw no formal withdrawal move, only demands for increased spending; even his most isolationist advisors rarely advocated full exit.
sources_consulted: Historical record of U.S. presidential actions on NATO
Credible media reporting on Trump-era NATO debates
